The target remains religion-centred under OER B2 and the underlying courses: traditions and sacred sources, empirical religious communities, esoteric cultural histories, myth and sacred images, secularisation, migration, new religious movements, popular culture and independent religious research. Arabic training is not used as an exclusion criterion. The repaired package does not narrow or change the independently verified Religious Studies core.

World Myth & Literature gives substantial cross-cultural narrative theory and primary materials; African art, archaeology and Ancient Democracy give religious visual/material meaning and ritual; Western art and Islamic Mediterranean exchanges add particular cultural contexts. Philosophical accounts of God, divine command and Buddhist selfhood, spiritual life writing, religious constitutions, freedom of religion and religion in reconciliation are also real. These bridges are stronger than the former blanket absence claims. The 43-course contribution ledger and three complete trials nevertheless show that expanding these bridges yields general humanities, social science or media/meaning study rather than a sustained response to religious traditions, sacred interpretation and lived contemporary religion. No numeric religion quota, exact-equivalence or licence requirement is applied. All trial schedules pass current offerings and prerequisites, so this judgment is academic.
